1.explanation: This script uses Lighthouse’s HTML renderer (jsdom + DetailsRenderer) to produce the same table you see in the report. We define two libraries—one whose transferSize divides evenly into KiB (18 × 1024 bytes) and one that does not (20.4 KiB). When you run the script (`node test-large-libraries-decimal.js`), you’ll see “18 KiB” (no decimal) next to date-fns, but “20.4 KiB” next to luxon, reproducing the bug. To fix it you’d change the byte-formatting utility (in util.js) to always render one decimal place, even when it is zero.
1.bug_scenario: In the “Large JavaScript libraries” details table, libraries whose transfer‐size in KiB is an integer (for example 18 KiB) are rendered without any decimal place ("18 KiB"), while non-integer sizes (for example 20.4 KiB) show one decimal. This misalignment makes it harder to scan the column.
